notes: SHIP v1.14.444 - R3: THE DEVICE FAMILIES STOP INVENTING STATE. WHAT R3 TURNED OUT TO BE. Section 11 asks for a small maintainable set of visual families. They already exist and have since v1.14.257 - eight kinds (compute, switch, power, patch, media, storage, blank, generic), each with a signature interior, drive bays and ports already drawn as InstancedMesh rather than loose geometry. So R3 was not a build. Reading those families against sections 5 and 34 found two things that should never have shipped, and fixing them is the entire ship. DEFECT 1, AND IT IS THE WORST IN THE RENDERER: THE SWITCH LIT ITS PORTS WITH Math.random. The line read if (Math.random() > 0.4) and lit roughly sixty percent of the ports. PHANTOM knows nothing about which ports are populated or live, so this was fabricated telemetry - and it was NON-DETERMINISTIC, reshuffling on every single re-render, so the same switch showed a different link pattern each time the rack was drawn. A technician reading lit ports as connected ports was reading dice. Contract 10, real data only. Replaced with a deterministic every-third-port pattern, the same representative treatment the patch panel already ships under John's ruling that representative geometry is not a count claim: it states this is a switch, never these ports are up. It is also cheaper - the old code minted up to about forty-eight individual sphere meshes per switch, the new one is thirty-two instances of a single geometry, so a dense switch costs one draw call instead of dozens. DEFECT 2: GREEN BLINKING LEDs CLAIMED PER-DEVICE HEALTH. Every drive bay, storage blade, media brick and PSU carried a green LED, and the greens pulsed from the animation loop. Green is PHANTOM's success colour under section 34, which says success only when actual state is success and not general decoration if it implies state; a blink is the universal signal for live activity. Eight blinking green LEDs across a drive bay cannot be read as anything but per-drive health, and PHANTOM receives no drive, blade or PSU telemetry at all. Section 5 is explicit that a green LED is permissible only if it cannot be read as operational health, and otherwise to prefer neutral dim white or blue. THE RULE THAT CAME OUT OF IT, written into the source so the next family does not re-litigate it: STATE colours (green, amber, red) may NOT be used decoratively because they mean something; ACCENT colours (cyan, violet, teal) MAY carry family identity because they claim nothing; and nothing blinks whatever its colour, because a blink is an activity claim on its own. So compute, storage, media and PSU lights became neutral cool white - the chassis still reads as manufactured hardware, it simply stops asserting a state - while the switch keeps its violet and the patch panel keeps its teal, which is exactly section 13's restrained violet and cyan secondary distinction. Implemented by aliasing greenLedMat and psuLedMat onto one neutral material, so four call sites changed with one edit and no churn. The blink list is now empty by design, which also removes per-frame material writes from the render loop (section 36). If real per-device status ever arrives, that neutral default is the seam a sourced status would override. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. Section 15 asks for a CDU and cooling family and PHANTOM has none - a CDU renders as power, because _TMAP maps cdu to pdu. That mapping is DELIBERATE and documented in the colour vocabulary, so changing it is a vocabulary change and belongs with defect D-3, which is already blocked on an owner ruling. Reported, not taken. Representative counts (eight drive bays, six PSUs, ten blades) are left alone - John already ruled representative geometry is not a count claim. No chassis colour, type colour, bezel strip, material, light, fog, tone-mapping or floor change. TESTS: new spec 31-renderer-data-honesty, four tests, and the primary one is PROVEN to catch the defect - re-injecting the random gate turns it red with 'a device family decides part of what it draws at random'. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SPEC ITSELF, WORTH RECORDING. First, the initial version grepped for randomness and failed against CORRECT code, because the fix's own comments quote the removed line verbatim; it now strips comments quote-aware before grepping. Second, and more important, a blanket no-randomness rule is simply WRONG - the scene also scatters dust motes at random, which is atmosphere and claims nothing about the Master. The assertion is now scoped to the device-family branches only: randomness is a defect when it decides what the rack DEPICTS, not when it places dust. A fourth test asserts violet SURVIVES, so the spec can never be satisfied by stripping every light off the rack and calling it honest. And the re-render census test is labelled in the source as CORROBORATING rather than the gate, because re-injecting the defect left it green - bw_render re-draws the existing scene rather than rebuilding trays, so it cannot vary. RUNS (phone-webkit): 31 + 30 + 29 + 20 + 22 = 26 passed. 02-build-forge alone = 14 passed. 08-forge-layout alone = 17 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .444. DEVICE-VERIFY: open BUILD with an active rack and look at the trays. PASS is families still telling each other apart - the switch violet, power shelves gold, GPU trays teal - with small neutral white lights and NOTHING pulsing. FAIL is any green dot, any blinking, or families that now look identical.
